module_title: Moderate Phase (1885-1905) - Policies, Leaders, and Economic Critique
introduction: At this level, we examine the Moderates' analysis of British policies. Although they failed to involve the masses, their greatest contribution was exposing the 'Economic Exploitation' of India by the British, laying a strong intellectual foundation for the future freedom struggle.

core_concepts.title: Drain of Wealth Theory
core_concepts.description: Propounded by Dadabhai Naoroji, this theory explained that the British were systematically draining India's wealth (via raw materials, salaries, and pensions) to Britain, which was the root cause of India's poverty.

core_concepts.title: Indian Councils Act 1892
core_concepts.description: This was a major political success for the Moderates. It increased the number of members in the legislative councils and gave Indian members the right to discuss the budget (though without the right to vote).

core_concepts.title: Limitations of Moderates
core_concepts.description: The movement was confined to the educated, urban middle class. They failed to understand the power of the masses and aimed for 'Dominion Status' (self-government under British rule) rather than 'Complete Independence'.

core_concepts.title: Demand for Civil Service Reforms
core_concepts.description: Moderates strongly demanded that the ICS (Indian Civil Service) examinations be held simultaneously in England and India, and that the maximum age limit be increased.

important_entities.name: Dadabhai Naoroji
important_entities.key_fact: Author of 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'
important_entities.significance: He officially presented the 'Drain of Wealth' theory in this landmark book.

important_entities.name: Gopal Krishna Gokhale
important_entities.significance: Founded the 'Servants of India Society' in 1905 to train Indians to dedicate their lives to the cause of the country.

important_entities.name: Surendranath Banerjee
important_entities.significance: Known as 'Rashtraguru'. He was one of the earliest Indians to clear the Civil Services examination but was unjustly dismissed.

important_entities.name: Badruddin Tyabji
important_entities.significance: Presided over the third Congress session held in Madras in 1887.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Remember, until 1905, the INC or Moderates NEVER demanded 'Purna Swaraj' (Complete Independence) or the expulsion of the British. They only wanted a share in the administration.
Under the 1892 Act, Indians got the right to 'discuss' the budget, but they were strictly denied the right to 'vote' on it or ask supplementary questions.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Remember these four to easily differentiate them from the Extremist leaders (Lal-Bal-Pal).

exam_strategy_tips: For 'Match the Following' questions, link authors to their books: Dadabhai Naoroji with 'Poverty and Un-British Rule', and R.C. Dutt with 'Economic History of India'.
Direct questions are often asked about the first Muslim President (Tyabji) and the first English/European President (George Yule, Allahabad session 1888).
